modules.comments:
Configuration from the process environment, as one typed record: the
variables a program needs are named and typed once, read in one go, and
every missing or malformed one is reported together. A `.env` file in the
working directory is read first, for development; a variable the
environment already has keeps its value.

    type Variables = ( "PORT" :: Maybe Int, "DB_PATH" :: String )

    main = Env.load (Proxy :: _ (Record Variables)) >>= case _ of
      Left errors -> throw (Env.printErrors errors)
      Right vars -> start vars

The two halves are modules of their own and are re-exported from here:
`Env.Dot` folds the file into the environment, `Env.Typed` reads the
record. `load` is the one call that does both.

Meant to be imported qualified: `Env.load`, `Env.read`, `Env.printErrors`.

declarations.comments:
The `.env` file in the working directory, if there is one, folded into
the process environment, and the variables the record names read from
it: `Env.Dot.environment` and `Env.Typed.read` in one.
declarations.title: load

modules.name: Env

declarations.comments:
Like `environment`, with the file named. A file that is not there is no
error; one that cannot be read (a directory, no permission) is thrown.
declarations.title: environmentFrom

declarations.comments:
The process environment after the `.env` file in the working directory
was folded into it.
declarations.title: environment

declarations.comments:
What stopped a record from being read: for each variable, that it is
missing (`EnvLookupError`) or does not parse (`EnvParseError`), by name.
At least one, or the record would have been read.
declarations.title: Errors

declarations.comments:
What went wrong with one variable: it is not set, or its text does not
parse, with the name and then the instance's reason.
declarations.title: EnvError

children.comments:
`true`, `yes`, `on`, `enabled` and `1`, or `false`, `no`, `off`, `disabled`
and `0`, in any case.
children.title: <anonymous>

declarations.comments:
How a variable's text becomes a value of the field's type. Write an
instance for a type of your own. A `Left` is the reason the text does not
parse, and completes the sentence `The variable "NAME" …`: "is not an
integer", "is not one of console, resend", "is empty".
declarations.title: ParseValue

declarations.comments:
Builds the record field by field from the row's list, collecting the
errors of every field instead of stopping at the first.
declarations.title: ReadRecord

declarations.comments:
Looks a variable up and parses it: a `Maybe` field may be missing, any
other has to be there. Exported because the compiler solves it where
`read` is called; there is nothing to write an instance of it for.
declarations.title: ReadVariable

declarations.comments:
The variables the record names, from an environment. Every field is a
variable: `"PORT" :: Int` has to be there and parse, `"PORT" :: Maybe Int`
may be missing but has to parse if it is there. A field of a type of your
own needs a `ParseValue` instance. All problems are reported together.
declarations.title: read

declarations.comments:
One message naming every variable in question, for a log or a stderr
line before exiting.
declarations.title: printErrors

modules.comments:
The `.env` half: a file of `KEY=value` lines folded into the process
environment, for development. A variable the environment already has
keeps its value, so a deployment's own environment always wins, and no
file is no error.

Node does the loading (`process.loadEnvFile`, through `node-process`), so
there is no parser here: the format is what Node accepts, `#` comments
and quoted values included, `${VAR}` expansion not.

declarations.comments:
The process environment after the `.env` file in the working directory
was folded into it.
declarations.title: environment
